source.title: Neural Complexity Measures
source.authors: Yoonho Lee; Juho Lee; Sung Ju Hwang; Eunho Yang; Seung-Jin Choi

record.tranche_reason: The study measures and predicts generalization gaps and tests a learned regularizer, using methods different from the claim versions. It does not test any version's specific intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own generalization-gap prediction, gap trends, and test-accuracy results for NC regularization and baselines. Cited results about complexity measures and dropout are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a learned generalization-gap predictor and regularizer, without testing any claim version. Its capacity comparisons do not establish a zero-training-error width threshold; its loss-surface visualizations do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps; its dropout experiments concern regression rather than classifiers.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that NC predicts generalization gaps, produces lower test than training loss when used as a regularizer, and transfers to previously unseen learner architectures and hyperparameters. They also report faster training and applicability to larger single classification tasks. Transfer is qualified by degraded prediction for substantially more expressive learners and no consistent regularization improvement for the four-layer learner.
record.recipe_differences: The study meta-learns a function to predict the generalization gap and uses it as a regularizer; the claim versions concern other training interventions, comparisons, and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: NC prediction accuracy degrades when the task learner is substantially more expressive (160 nodes and 4 layers); NC regularization does not consistently improve test loss when the architecture differs substantially (4 layers). On SVHN, NC is below label smoothing and Mixup.

fits_no_version.finding: NC predicts sinusoid-regression generalization gaps with R² = 0.9589.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A meta-learned function can predict generalization gaps from data and learner predictions.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report test loss below training loss throughout NC-regularized learning in their tested settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NC regularization can produce negative generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: NC improves mean accuracy over unregularized cross-entropy on all five image datasets, but on SVHN falls below L2, label smoothing and Mixup.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learned gap predictor used as a regularizer can improve classification accuracy, with advantages depending on dataset and comparator.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller KMNIST training sets exhibit more severe overfitting, and NC estimates capture this trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NC can track variation in generalization gaps across training-set sizes.

record.problems: The paper reports figures without exact values for some learning curves and transfer comparisons. NC's single-task image-classification evaluation uses no image augmentation or manual learning-rate scheduling, limiting those results to the stated setup.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were applicable. Figure-only test-loss and transfer results in Figures 5, 10, and 12 were not added because precise values are not stated in the text. Table 2 sinusoid-regression dropout results were not extracted as evidence for V6, which concerns classifiers.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural labels under the same architecture and recipe.
Test-error trends when widening beyond the width required for zero training error. Increasing pooled-network capacity does not establish this threshold or comparison.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers on the same image tasks, including effects of local connectivity and initialization.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on classifier test error, including small-data, excessive-dropout and augmentation conditions. Table 2 and Figure 14 evaluate sinusoid regression.
Association of magnitude-aware sharpness with generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Normalized loss-surface visualizations do not supply that comparison.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. All rows concern results outside V1–V8; their states are therefore cannot_determine relative to these versions, without disputing the reported findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Whether widening past the zero-training-error threshold lowers test error.
A controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected learners on image tasks.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects in fully connected or convolutional classifiers, including the specified training-set and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its comparative ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
